tables.label: tab:procedures
tables.title: Timing procedures and reference settings
tables.caption:
Timing procedures and their prescribed reference settings. Both procedures
solve each inactive system with Algorithm~\ref{alg:revision_deflation}, including its
residual replacement, and restrict the reference on the GPU. Complete temporal coverage
keeps every temporal factor of each retained spatial mode; truncated coverage keeps the
lowest spatial--temporal pairs up to the total rank. Temporal coverage does not apply to
steady cases.

tables.label: tab:mesh_complete
tables.title: Primary complete optimization costs
tables.caption:
Median complete-sequence times in seconds over five repetitions of 16-target
optimization sequences; every method converges at every target in every repetition.
The speedup is the ratio of the median times of the fastest alternative and RefDef; brackets give the envelope of ratios between extreme repetition times. Dimension counts the optimized spatial or space--time
DOFs. RefDef and recycling use total rank 100, and the transformer uses the
skew-symmetric transport \eqref{eq:skew_transport}.

tables.label: tab:cht_transfer
tables.title: Matched Cartesian transfer replays
tables.caption:
Matched replays of direct restriction and zero-extension transfer of the
full-domain reference on the same systems with zero initial guesses. Time
and iterations sum per-kernel medians over three repetitions. Solves counts the
replayed inactive systems, Rank gives the smallest and largest retained rank over these
solves, and Energy fraction is the median of
Equation~\eqref{eq:coarse_energy_fraction}.

tables.label: tab:v20_scale
tables.title: Steady scale comparisons
tables.caption:
Steady comparisons under Algorithm~\ref{alg:final_procedure} with 16 targets.
Times are median complete-sequence seconds over the repetitions, out of five, that
converge at every target. The speedup is the ratio of the median times of the fastest
alternative and RefDef, and brackets give the envelope of ratios between
extreme repetition times; the iteration ratio divides
the median inner iterations of Jacobi-CG by those of RefDef, and a dash
marks a ratio without a converged Jacobi-CG repetition. The last column lists each
method with a repetition that fails to converge, with its converged and attempted
repetitions. The standard AmgX stopping factor is $10^{-1}$; AmgX ($10^{-2}$) and AmgX
($10^{-3}$) set it to $10^{-2}$ and $10^{-3}$. The $96^3$ and Bore~4 envelopes combine
measurements from separate jobs. $^\dagger$Compared with a subset of the alternatives: Bore~4
with Jacobi-CG and AmgX, where PDAS may take up to 400 steps.

tables.label: tab:v20_transient
tables.title: Trajectory comparisons
tables.caption:
Trajectory comparisons optimize all slabs of the horizon at once. Columns
follow Table~\ref{tab:v20_scale}, and unknowns count all slabs. The Cartesian references
keep $S=12$ spatial modes, each with a temporal factor for every slab, at eight slabs and $S=6$ at 16 and 32 slabs, and the
transformer uses the skew-symmetric transport. $^\dagger$Compared with Jacobi-CG alone.

tables.label: tab:v20_operation
tables.title: Operating sequences
tables.caption:
Operating sequences change loads, flow rates, windows or query order; one
reference built at nominal conditions is used for every query. Columns follow
Table~\ref{tab:v20_scale}, and the transformer uses the skew-symmetric transport in
every sequence.

tables.label: si:tab_transport_certificates
tables.title: Transport energy stability
tables.caption:
Inertia of $\tfrac12(K_{FF}+K_{FF}^\top)$, the symmetric part of the assembled
free-node matrix. Counts give negative, zero and positive eigenvalues. The transport-negative
column counts the negative eigenvalues of the symmetric part $S$ of the free-node transport
matrix alone, after adding $\sigma(C_\ell)_{FF}$ with
$\sigma=10^{-9}\max|S|/\max(C_\ell)_{FF}$, which separates a semidefinite part from an
indefinite one. The last column states whether the symmetric part of $K_{FF}$ is
positive definite, which rules out growing modes; Table~\ref{si:tab_v20_temporal} shows
the growth of the original transformer transport.

tables.label: si:tab_experiment_map
tables.title: Comparison inventory
tables.caption:
Comparisons, problems and measurements. Every timed comparison
uses 16 targets and five complete sequence repetitions per method unless
stated otherwise. Ranks denote total spatial or space--time rank, and $S$
the number of spatial modes, each paired with a temporal factor for every slab.

tables.label: si:tab_amgx_configuration
tables.title: AmgX configuration
tables.caption:
The complete steady and transient comparisons use the
same AmgX hierarchy settings. Original inactive systems use the absolute
target $10^{-11}\|b\|_2$, with $10^{-11}$ used when $b=0$.
The separate correction protocol in Section~\ref{si:mesh_refinement_diagnosis}
specifies error-equation targets and remaining iteration budgets.

tables.label: si:tab_timing_definitions
tables.title: Timing boundaries
tables.caption:
The timing intervals partition the measured complete
optimization sequence. Their sum equals the complete time.
Preparation costs use separate enclosing process measurements.

tables.label: si:tab_mesh_validation
tables.title: Independent body-fitted verification
tables.caption:
Independent bounded-variable least squares verifies the
mesh PDAS solutions. State and objective errors are relative to
the independent solution. KKT is the largest of the five stated
KKT components of the PDAS solution, and Dimension counts the optimized DOFs. Uniform and unequal entries denote complete
two-slab optimizations.

tables.label: si:tab_cht_validation
tables.title: Independent Cartesian verification
tables.caption:
Independent bounded least squares corroborates
the complete PDAS solutions. The last three columns give
maxima across the three PDAS solvers for each problem.
Query indices 0, 1 and 2 correspond to
$\theta=0,1/2,1$. KKT entries are the largest of
the five quantities defined in the main protocol.

tables.label: si:tab_v20_temporal
tables.title: Time refinement and replay
tables.caption:
Time refinement and replay of the optimized trajectories. The verified column
counts discrete optimizations, over all slab counts, that meet the residual and KKT
criteria, agree with a direct-PDAS solution at the coarsest slab count, and whose
forward replays on 128 and 256 steps are solved to the residual tolerance; it does not
establish feasibility between time levels. The difference columns give the largest and root-mean-square temperature
difference between the eight-slab and 64-slab optima. Replay change and exceedance are
diagnostics of the eight-slab controls, and the last column of the 64-slab controls. A
dash marks a quantity without a verified optimization or without a replay. The
bore-in-block advective operator is energy-stable
(Table~\ref{si:tab_transport_certificates}). All temperatures are in kelvin.

tables.label: si:tab_mesh_work
tables.title: Complete timing ranges and GPU allocation
tables.caption:
Complete time and sampled GPU allocation of the primary body-fitted
comparisons. Each cell gives the median time in seconds, the observed range
over the converged repetitions, and the maximum sampled GPU allocation in gibibytes (GiB),
in that order. A count in parentheses gives converged and attempted
repetitions when they differ. Rank is the requested reference or recycling rank.

tables.label: si:tab_cht_accuracy
tables.title: Cartesian residual and KKT maxima
tables.caption:
The residual and KKT maxima cover the 300 complete Cartesian
sequences of Section~\ref{si:cht_complete_results}.
The columns give
the original relative linear residual and maxima of
stationarity, primal feasibility, dual feasibility,
complementarity and projected gradient. Primal feasibility
is absolute; the other KKT quantities use the normalization
in the main protocol.

tables.label: si:tab_mesh_transfer
tables.title: Matched body-fitted transfer replays
tables.caption:
Matched mesh replays measure the information supplied by
two specified transfers. Each trace replays the first repetition of the corresponding
sequence of main Table~\Mref{tab:mesh_complete}; the transformer trace uses the
skew-symmetric transport. Systems counts the inactive systems of each trace;
activated and released count constraint changes after the first restriction,
including those between queries. Energy fraction is the median initial energy-error fraction
removed by the coarse correction. Iterations and
time sum the per-kernel medians over the sampled systems, and Kernels counts these
systems.
Each kernel has three repetitions, all meeting the residual criterion.

tables.label: si:tab_small_spectrum
tables.title: Deflated spectra of small replays
tables.caption:
Median condition numbers of the small matched replays in Jacobi-scaled
coordinates: the original preconditioned matrix and the deflated operator after each
transfer.

tables.label: si:tab_retention_ablation
tables.title: Complete-sequence retention ablation
tables.caption:
Complete-sequence retention ablation. Times are median complete-sequence
seconds over five repetitions of 16 targets. The ratio divides the median time of
zero-extension transfer by that of direct restriction; brackets give the envelope of
ratios between extreme repetition times. The iteration ratio divides their median inner
iterations.

tables.label: si:tab_cht_conditioning
tables.title: Conditional conditioning certificates
tables.caption:
Controlled $6^3$ CHT restrictions distinguish
angle bounds from conditioning-improvement certificates.
Every row retains rank one. The columns give removed
nodes $q$, minimum restricted singular value $\sigma$,
subspace residual, separation, actual largest-angle
sine, sufficient angle bound $\epsilon$, original
condition number, predicted upper bound $K$ and
measured effective condition number.

tables.label: si:tab_v20_comparisons
tables.title: Supplementary sensitivity comparisons
tables.caption:
Supplementary comparisons under the procedure and criteria of main
Section~\Mref{sec:v20_results}. Columns follow main Table~\Mref{tab:v20_scale}:
times are median complete-sequence seconds over the converged repetitions, brackets
give the envelope of ratios between extreme repetition times, and the last column
gives converged and
attempted repetitions of each method that fails to converge in some repetition.
$^\dagger$Compared with Jacobi-CG alone, or on Bore~4 with Jacobi-CG and AmgX. Level
0 denotes the packaged mesh and level $\ell$ its $\ell$-th refinement. Unless the
setting names a reference level or rank, the transformer and Bore~2 rows use the
packaged-mesh reference with total rank 100, and the Bore~3 rows use the packaged-mesh
reference with rank 200; the sorted rows and the four-method Bore~3 row give the
matching nominal comparisons. The Bore~4 envelope combines measurements from separate
jobs.

tables.label: si:tab_v20_single
tables.title: Single-repetition and solver-limit comparisons
tables.caption:
Single-repetition comparisons at the longest horizons and the solver
limits. Columns follow main Table~\Mref{tab:v20_scale}; each row times one sequence
per method, so the speedup is a single ratio without an envelope. The rows with $S=4$
and $S=6$ time RefDef in a separate job from the alternatives.

tables.label: si:tab_v20_direct
tables.title: CPU direct and block-in-time comparisons
tables.caption:
CPU factorization solvers beside the GPU comparisons of the same problems.
Entries are median complete-sequence seconds over five 16-target repetitions. Block
denotes the block-in-time CG of the main protocol, and a dash marks a steady problem.

tables.label: si:tab_temperature_bounds
tables.title: Optimized fields under different bounds
tables.caption:
The optimized Bore 1 fields satisfy three upper temperature bounds.
Extrema and active fractions cover all optimized state DOFs.
The tracking error uses the spatial or space--time objective weights.
Temperatures and errors are dimensionless; the active fraction is a percentage.

tables.label: si:tab_original_transport
tables.title: Earlier advective transformer comparisons
tables.caption:
Transformer comparisons with the original advective transport, whose
operator has growing modes. Columns follow main Table~\Mref{tab:v20_scale}.

tables.label: si:tab_mesh_correction
tables.title: Earlier residual-correction comparisons
tables.caption:
Residual-correction comparisons preserve the finer-transformer
four-target problems and final accuracy requirements. Complete sequences
and target solves are counted separately. Times give the median and
observed range in seconds over five complete repetitions. Residual and KKT
columns give maxima across completed sequences; corrections count all
error equations.
